content.goal: Enable an obstacle-detection module for a small indoor robot that detects objects in front of it and issues timely reactions before collisions, while confirming detection range, reaction latency, robot-controller interface behavior, and indoor safety assumptions before component selection.
content.problemStatement: The initial obstacle-detection module requires a functional architecture, but key constraints for detection range/field of view, maximum reaction latency, robot-controller interface semantics, and indoor fail-safe safety assumptions are not yet confirmed. The prototype must remain non-component-specific until these unknowns are resolved.
content.intendedContext: An early-stage team will prototype the module, test obstacle detection and reaction timing in indoor scenarios, and review analysis-ready outputs to decide next embedded constraints.
scope: Functional specification for obstacle sensing, obstacle interpretation, and reaction decision behavior.
Functional design for timestamped obstacle evidence logging and safety-focused control behavior.
Explicit identification of unknown obstacle range, reaction latency, interface behavior, and indoor safety constraints.
outOfScope: Component-part selection (specific sensor models, MCUs, cameras, lidars, or control algorithms).
Firmware libraries, PCB layout, schematic validation, and simulation execution.
Production manufacturing planning and deployment infrastructure.
successCriteria: All produced artifacts conform to the v1 contracts.
Explicit and inferred requirements are distinguishable.
Unsupported assumptions are not presented as facts.
The Next Action is derived from concrete blockers and open questions about obstacle-detection needs.

assumptions.statement: Indoor obstacle-avoidance behavior can be evaluated using functional architecture outputs without assuming specific component technologies in this phase.
